status: profiled; optimization proposal awaits review; default remains held
scope: Node host-input inspectCoreElementKind on the pinned 820-byte input; final per-runtime-schema implementation

method.runWindow: Sampler began about 3.8 seconds after process start, after the measured ~3.1-second factory setup; sampled process was the isolated operation loop.

findings.interpretation: Source document validation, especially recursive constraint-program evaluation, dominates the sampled call stack. The stack counts are inclusive and overlap; they are not additive stage timings. Host reflection and copy code appear in the sample but are lower-volume. Wire encode and result-envelope symbols appear only in a handful of samples. The earlier instrumented stage split on the same operation path placed host source copy around 11–12 ms, document validation around 13–15 ms, operation-result schema validation under 0.4 ms, and output encoding around 0.1 ms; schema compilation was removed from per-call work and is factory-owned in the current binary.
findings.hostReflection: The existing instrumented run counted 291 host dispatches per operation. The no-meter sample shows NodeHostJson::reflect and copy_host_json activity, but not at the volume of document validation.

meterCallbackExperiment.interpretation: An explicitly configured JS meter callback has a large cross-boundary cost in this diagnostic. The benchmarked default operation path provides no meter callback; this result should be treated as a separate opt-in-controls cost.

optimizationProposal.target: The repeated recursive interpretation of the immutable core constraint program in constraints::exec / constraints::eval during Engine::validate_document.

minimalPlanDesign.representation: A per-runtime side table keyed by immutable PreparedProgram node path/ordinal. It stores only checked static discriminants (StepKind and ExprKind), and child/field ordinals for fields already validated by constraint_language::check_program. It does not copy evaluated values, collapse nodes, reorder children, cache data-derived results, or alter the existing Value tree. A lightweight prototype may first cache only op enum plus validated field ordinals; no bytecode VM is proposed.

steps.allowedUse: Replace repeated get(step, "op") + UTF-16-to-String dispatch and fixed-name get(step, field) lookups with the prevalidated discriminant/ordinal. Preserve the current step visitation and field evaluation order exactly.

expressions.allowedUse: For validated expression nodes, cache whether the checked node is a var, op, or object constructor, the checked opcode enum, and child/member ordinals. This only removes repeated shape/op/member dispatch. Recursively evaluate the same operands through the existing runtime helpers in the same order.

explicitExclusions: Do not precompute source/document/policy values or branch outcomes.
Do not pre-expand for/filter/map/find/some/every/index loops or change their short-circuit order.
Do not pre-evaluate and/or operands; retain short-circuiting.
Do not cache environment lookup results, paths, enumerations, sorts, canonical forms, diagnostics, extension registry results, or callback outputs.
Do not compile dynamic strings into host callbacks or bypass Runtime conversion/copy helpers.
If an operation or future AST shape is not in the checked static allowlist, keep the current interpreter/refusal path; never silently map unknown content to a no-op.

accountingAndDynamicBoundaries.perVisitedNode: constraints::exec charges ctx.charge_constraint_step(Utf16::default()) then fires observer("constraint-instruction", 1) before reading/dispatching each visited step (constraints.rs:2551-2566). constraints::eval does the same before each visited expression (constraints.rs:1324-1338). The plan must preserve those calls at the same node entry, including nodes revisited in loops and short-circuit paths; no batched, setup-time, or skipped per-call charge is acceptable.
accountingAndDynamicBoundaries.observerSites: Exact observer call sites: constraint-value-visit in runtime-copy/value traversal helpers (around 49 and 1829), constraint-instruction after each eval/exec charge_constraint_step (1337 and 2565), constraint-enumeration before keys/values/entries (1432), without (1528), and flatten (1598), plus constraint-sort after sort's value-visit estimate (1832). Preserve each computed amount and its placement relative to Context charges, copies, and callbacks; do not infer observer amounts at setup.
dynamicBoundaries: Input-derived Runtime values and lexical environment lookup/mutation.
for and collection cardinality, iteration, early exit, and per-iteration environment clone/copy.
Map mutation, duplicate-key checks, canonicalization and sorting.
Registry and Capabilities extension validation; callback return values, errors, and exception provenance.
Context cancellation, maxWork, meter callback, and observer outcomes.

expectedBound.sampleBasis: constraints::exec is 1182/2749 = 43.0% inclusive samples; the count overlaps its parents and is not a wall-time fraction. The stage probe attributes about 13–15 ms of the ~27 ms operation to source validation, including constraint work.
expectedBound.absoluteAmdahlCeiling: Even the impossible removal of every sampled exec frame would imply only about 1.75x speedup if the sample fraction approximated CPU time (1 / (1 - 0.43)); this is a loose ceiling, not a target or prediction.
expectedBound.realisticStaticDispatchBound: The proposed plan retains recursive traversal, expression evaluation, dynamic Runtime operations, and all accounting. Until measured, expect single-digit improvement; use 1.20x (20% reduction in operation time) as a conservative upper bound for static lookup/dispatch alone. A result above that requires a new profile showing that repeated static lookup dominates. No speedup is guaranteed.

focusedDifferentialPlan.oracle: Run the existing interpreter and candidate plan on identical immutable PreparedProgram, source, identity, resources, factory controls, and fresh per-call Context; compare exact outputs/errors and complete Context/observer traces.
focusedDifferentialPlan.diagnostics: Pin exact diagnostic list order, code, message, path, severity and metadata for let/for/if/emit/remember plus each diagnostic-producing expression. Include the current six frozen operation packet cases.
focusedDifferentialPlan.meterAndCancellation: Capture ordered meter amounts/paths and observer events for normal execution; inject refusal at every distinct charge boundary around node entry, env clone, enumeration, sort and diagnostic creation. Compare first error class and callback order. Cancel at each reachable node/iteration boundary and verify no later observer, meter, callback, or diagnostic event occurs.
focusedDifferentialPlan.unknownContent: Exercise unknown step/expression opcode, extra field, unknown opaque payload nested in ordinary document data, and extension payload with empty/default Registry. Verify the same refusal or preservation as the oracle; verify registered callback behavior remains dynamically invoked with identical order and exception provenance.
focusedDifferentialPlan.hostAndBrowser: Replay existing frozen hostile current/source/identity/request/accessor/proxy/refusal controls in Bun against the actual installed Node addon. Then rebuild an isolated fresh WASM artifact and repeat the complete focused packet in real Chromium. Assert exact trace/result parity, not just success. Record source/artifact hashes and browser version in receipts.
focusedDifferentialPlan.performance: Measure setup separately from warmed operation latency on the pinned 820-byte source, at least 30 calls per route and multiple alternating runs. Report median and p95, plus inclusive profile counts. Reject the optimization if any semantics/control trace changes or if the upper-bound target is not achieved without increasing setup/refusal cost materially.

optimizationProposal.reviewGate: Read-only refinement only; no production edits are included. Implement only after integrated source cohort stabilizes and reviewers approve the equivalence boundary. Keep default selection held until exact differential traces, fresh Chromium parity, resource/accounting checks, and benchmark all pass and Sol accepts the evidence.
